subject: Silverline renewal: structured ramp, EU region add, and price corridor negotiation
messages:
From: Alex Gonzales <alex@silverline.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@silverline.io
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal request + capacity expansion (dec 1 renewal)

Hi Vanessa —

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for Silverline (contract expires Dec 1) is coming up and we need a quote that reflects two changes:

1) We plan to increase committed monthly token throughput ~3x next year to support a new product launch (mainly text gen and embeddings).
2) We’re launching in the EU region and want a price-floor/hold for the first 2 quarters while we ramp traffic to avoid volatility during launch.

Can Redwood propose a renewal that:
- Includes a phased ramp (commit schedule month-by-month or quarter-by-quarter)
- Holds the per-token price for Q1–Q2 in EU at the current US list for the first 6 months (or a negotiated corridor)
- Provides a credit/true-up mechanism if we miss the committed floor in the first year

Procurement also needs SOC 2 evidence and a rough PO timeline (we’d like to issue PO by Nov 20). I’ve attached our Q3 usage so you can see baseline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Alex
Head of Platform — Silverline
Alex.Gonzales@silverline.io

Attachment: Q3-usage-report.csv
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gonzales <alex@silverline.io>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal request + capacity expansion (dec 1 renewal)

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. We can absolutely structure a renewal that smooths launch risk for EU and supports an increased commit. High level proposal attached (Proposed_Termsheet_Silverline_v1.pdf). Key bullets:

- Three-phase commit ramp (months 1–3: 1.5x baseline, months 4–6: 2.5x, months 7–12: 3x).
- EU launch corridor: hold current US list price for EU traffic for first two fiscal quarters after go-live OR provide a capped uplift of +5% vs US list if needed for capacity economics.
- Missed floor credit: if actual monthly consumption is below 80% of committed for any quarter during first year, we provide a prorated credit applied to the following invoice (one-time true-up credit).
- Overage tiers: staged overage pricing with softer first-tier surcharge (to avoid surprise bills during launch).

Next steps I recommend: finance model to validate margin at different commit levels and a conditional approval from Sales leadership for introductory EU concession. I’ve looped in David for the pricing model. If this looks directionally OK, I’ll prepare a term sheet + PO-ready doc for Nov 15.

Happy to take a 30m call tomorrow.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: Proposed_Termsheet_Silverline_v1.pdf
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Silverline pricing math and concession options (D-2027-3485)

Vanessa / Marissa —

I reviewed Alex’s ask and Vanessa’s term-sheet. I built a short model (attached) with three options:

A) Ramp + EU price hold (Vanessa’s outline). Margin impact: ~4.2% on blended tokens in Y1.
B) Upfront commit (12-month prepay at 1.1x of annual committed spend) for a 10% upfront discount to list — improves cash and reduces margin hit to ~7.8%.
C) Hybrid: 6-month price hold + graduated rebate tied to realized monthly % of committed (0–3% rebate band) — slightly better margin than A, preserves flexibility for Silverline.

I recommend option C for negotiation; it gives Silverline launch protection while limiting our downside. If Sales wants to offer a higher introductory discount for EU traffic (Alex asked for 12%), we need explicit sign-off from Revenue Ops for any concession >10% in the first year.

Attachment: silverline_commit_model.xlsx

David
Director, Pricing & Revenue Strategy
From: Alex Gonzales <alex@silverline.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@silverline.io
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal request + capacity expansion (dec 1 renewal)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick proposal. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) We prefer a corridor approach (your capped +5% uplift is ok) but would like the option of a 12% introductory discount on EU traffic for the first 9 months to help with vendor parity in Europe.
2) For the credit, we prefer a quarterly true-up (rather than a one-time credit) so our books reconcile in shorter windows.
3) EU SLA request: 99.5% availability for the EU region for model-serving endpoints, with a 1-week remediation SLA for regional incidents — can Redwood include that in the term sheet or point to an existing regional SLA addendum?

Procurement: we can issue PO Nov 20 if we can get an updated term sheet and SOC 2 evidence this week. Also happy to sign as soon as docuSign is ready.

If you can move on the EU discount to 12% for 9 months, we’ll commit to the 3x monthly throughput target by month 12 and sign a 12-month term.

Best,
Alex

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 15:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal approval for Silverline concession (D-2027-3485)

Vanessa / David —

I’m okay to approve a limited EU concession but with tightened guardrails. Approval notes:

- Approved concession: 10% introductory discount on EU traffic for the first 9 months (not 12%).
- Required customer commitment: Silverline must sign a 12-month renewal and increase committed monthly throughput to a minimum 3.0x baseline by month 12. If they fail to reach the 3.0x commit by month 12, the introductory discount is clawed back pro rata.
- Credits/true-ups: we’ll support quarterly true-ups (customer preference). Credits will apply to the subsequent invoice, limited to a maximum of 15% of that invoice value per quarter.
- EU SLA: Sales Ops to include the regional SLA addendum (99.5% availability). If customer requires a stricter SLA, route to Legal for a tailored amendment.
- Concession cap: total expected revenue concession not to exceed 12% of projected Y1 revenue under the selected option (C preferred).

Vanessa — please update the term sheet reflecting 10% EU discount (9 months), quarterly true-ups, and the SLA addendum reference. Circulate the updated PDF to Alex and procurement and include the DocuSign link. Once Alex confirms PO timing we’ll finalize.

Marissa
VP, Revenue (Redwood Inference)
